text:
maya: Quick sync — I want to update the reranker evals before the next canary. Thinking about changing the holdout sampling strategy. current split is random from logs which skews to popular queries.

josh: yep we should stratify. lots of tail queries never appear, so random favors head.

eli: can you sketch the goal? distribution match to production traffic or to human label distribution?

maya: main goal is twofold: 1) ensure we detect regressions on long-tail/formatted queries, 2) keep a small human-labeled set that reflects real error modes. so blend production-weighted sample + targeted strata for troublesome buckets.

samira: agree. propose strata: query length (tokens), click-rate bucket (head/mid/tail), and intent class (nav/qa/transactional). we can oversample tail and low-ctr queries for detection power.

ben: how big is the current human set? 3k? we might need ~5-7k if we oversample slices to get decent NDCG variance.

maya: current human labeled = 3200 queries. if we do stratified sampling with oversample factor 3 on tails we'd aim for ~6k. budget ok?

clare: for metrics: we still report NDCG@10 and MRR@10 but need to add per-stratum NDCG and delta-by-stratum. global NDCG can hide regressions.

josh: +1. Also compute bootstrap CI and report p-values. Not comfortable with single-point deltas.

maya: agreed. let's use pairwise bootstrap on queries (1000 resamples) and compute 95% CI for delta. if CI excludes 0 mark as significant.

eli: small ask: ensure dedupe across folds. we sometimes leak same query-doc pair via slight url variants -> inflates scores. Need canonical doc id and aggressive de-dupe.

samira: noted. I'll run dedupe heuristics: canonicalize host/path, strip tracking params, fuzzy title match for near-duplicates.

eval-bot: test-run complete: baseline vs quant-llm-ranker-8bit (sample subset 1). NDCG@10 delta = -0.012 (CI: -0.018, -0.006) p=0.002 -> significant regression on head.

ben: hmm quantized model shows regressions on head but maybe not tail? need stratified report.

maya: can you dump per-stratum numbers, bot?

eval-bot: per-stratum summary (NDCG@10 delta): head = -0.015 (CI -0.022, -0.008), mid = -0.004 (CI -0.011, 0.003), tail = +0.006 (CI -0.003, 0.015).

clare: interesting — tail improved slightly but head got worse. could be quantization sensitivity for high-frequency tokens or soft max calibration.

eli: also check ranking calibration: score distribution shifted? If top-1 scores collapse, MRR suffers. add KL or shift metric.

maya: good point. add mean score delta and top-k score gap.

samira: operational note: our production holdout is impression-weighted. if we change eval sampling we'll need to keep an impression-weighted metric in the pipeline for deployment decisions. so 2 views: production-weighted metric (for business impact) + stratified human set (for safety/regression detection).

josh: for dataset selection: let's keep a small curated TREC-like set (hard relevance judgments) for absolute checks, plus the stratified human-labeled set, plus an ongoing streaming implicit-feedback test (daily AUC/NDCG on impression logs).

maya: rollout policy: if production-weighted NDCG delta <= -0.005 -> block. if production-weighted delta within [-0.005, 0.005] but any stratum shows significant regression -> fail canary and require tradeoff doc (why tail/head differ).

ben: sounds practical. one more: query/doc formatting differences can change scores — we should freeze preprocessing and log the exact preproc hash used for each eval. otherwise small tokenization changes can look like model regressions.

clare: +1. pin tokenization version and truncation policy. note: for long docs we truncate to 512 tokens currently; maybe test 1024 for long-context rerankers.

eli: on significance testing: prefer multi-metric correction (we'll test many strata) — use Benjamini-Hochberg at 10% FDR to avoid overcounting.

maya: good call. add FDR correction to the pipeline.

samira: I'll update the eval spec and create a sampling job: stratified sampling job + dedupe + preproc hash + label scheduling to reach target ~6k labels.

maya: thanks. timeline?

samira: I can run the sampling and start labeling next week. aim to have initial stratified results + CI by Thu.

josh: i'll prepare the canary gate changes and the CI code (bootstraps + FDR) — will test on synthetic diffs.

maya: awesome. last thing: let's log an example of failure modes when head regresses but tail improves so we have runbook entries for product owners.

clare: will draft runbook once we have per-stratum outputs.

maya: cool. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
